title: Almost orthogonal bases for finite-dimensional ultrametric normed spaces
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a complete, nontrivial, nonarchimedean real absolute value $|\cdot|$: it is multiplicative, vanishes precisely at zero, has $|1|=1$, satisfies $|a+b|\le\max(|a|,|b|)$, and some nonzero $a$ has $|a|\ne1$. Completeness is for the metric $d(a,b)=|a-b|$. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], with $n=\dim_K V$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], and with a function $\|\cdot\|:V\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ satisfying $\|v\|=0\Longleftrightarrow v=0$, $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$ and $\|v+w\|\le\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$. For every real $0<r<1$, there is a $K$-basis $(e_i)_{1\le i\le n}$ of $V$ such that, for every $(a_i)_{1\le i\le n}\in K^n$, $$r\max_{1\le i\le n}(|a_i|\|e_i\|)\le\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n a_i e_i\right\|.$$ For $n=0$ the basis is empty, and the empty maximum and sum are both zero.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.3, printed p. 48, choice of an r-orthogonal basis and its displayed defining inequality; the existence input is explicitly attributed there to Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, Non-Archimedean Analysis, 2.6.1/3.

proof.text: Equip $V$ with $d(v,w)=\|v-w\|$. Definiteness and the ultrametric inequality make this a Hausdorff metric. Addition and negation are continuous by $\|(v+w)-(v_0+w_0)\|\le\max(\|v-v_0\|,\|w-w_0\|)$ and $\|-v\|=\|v\|$. Scalar multiplication is continuous by $\|av-bw\|\le\max(|a|\|v-w\|,|a-b|\|w\|)$, with $|a|\le\max(|b|,|a-b|)$ locally bounded. Thus $V$ is a Hausdorff topological $K$-vector space.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.3, printed p. 48, r-orthogonal basis input (BGR 2.6.1/3); agent-written dimension-induction proof of this input.

proof.text: Induct on $n$, with the assertion quantified over every normed space of dimension $n$ and every $0<r<1$. At $n=0$ use the empty basis. For $n>0$, discard successively any vector in the span of its predecessors from a finite spanning family; the remaining independent spanning family is a basis of $n$ elements. Let $W$ span its first $n-1$ elements and let $z$ be its last element. Then $V=W\oplus Kz$ and $\dim W=n-1$. Put $s=(1+r)/2$; then $0<s<1$ and $s^2-r=(1-r)^2/4>0$. The induction hypothesis gives an $s$-orthogonal basis $(e_i)_{i<n}$ of $W$ with its restricted norm.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.3, printed p. 48, r-orthogonal basis input (BGR 2.6.1/3); agent-written dimension-induction proof of this input.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-subspace-closed], $W$ is closed: the field is complete and nontrivially normed, the ambient space is Hausdorff and has continuous vector-space operations by step 1, and $W$ is finite-dimensional. Since $z\notin W$, some ball of radius $\epsilon>0$ about $z$ misses $W$. Hence $\delta=\inf_{w\in W}\|z-w\|\ge\epsilon>0$; the infimum exists since the set is nonempty and bounded below. Because $\delta/s>\delta$, the definition of infimum gives $w_0\in W$ with $\|z-w_0\|<\delta/s$. Set $e=z-w_0$. Then $V=W\oplus Ke$ and $s\|e\|<\delta$.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.3, printed p. 48, r-orthogonal basis input (BGR 2.6.1/3); agent-written dimension-induction proof of this input.

proof.text: For $w\in W$ and $a\ne0$, one has $\|w+ae\|=|a|\|z-(w_0-a^{-1}w)\|\ge|a|\delta>s|a|\|e\|$. If $\|w\|>|a|\|e\|$, the two ultrametric inequalities for $w+ae$ and $w=(w+ae)-ae$ force $\|w+ae\|=\|w\|$. Otherwise the preceding lower bound gives $\|w+ae\|\ge s\max(\|w\|,|a|\|e\|)$. The same weak inequality holds when $a=0$, directly from $s<1$.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.3, printed p. 48, r-orthogonal basis input (BGR 2.6.1/3); agent-written dimension-induction proof of this input.

proof.text: Write $w=\sum_{i<n}a_i e_i$ and $M=\max_{i<n}|a_i|\|e_i\|$, taking $M=0$ for an empty index set. The induction hypothesis gives $\|w\|\ge sM$, so step 4 yields $\|w+ae\|\ge s\max(sM,|a|\|e\|)\ge s^2\max(M,|a|\|e\|)\ge r\max(M,|a|\|e\|)$. The family $(e_1,\ldots,e_{n-1},e)$ is a basis because $e=z-w_0$ replaces the last vector of the chosen basis by subtracting an element of $W$. This proves the induction and the required inequality.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.3, printed p. 48, r-orthogonal basis input (BGR 2.6.1/3); agent-written dimension-induction proof of this input.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q48-5369f40c6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and all five steps in full. The statement is byte-identical to the base (unsplit) copy in the Q36 snapshot, and there are no new nodes. I could not check the source at the cited place: the Temkin PDF (Lemma 6.3.3, p.48) is not in the local literature. The statement is the standard r-orthogonal-basis existence over a complete, nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field, and I verified it independently through the proof. The only citer, lem-trf-analytic-close-embedding-degree step 1, applies it to H/A with r=(1+c)/2, and every hypothesis holds there. Step 1: the metric is Hausdorff and addition and scalar multiplication are continuous, including continuity at b=0 and w=0. Step 2: the induction is quantified over all spaces and all r, and s=(1+r)/2 gives s²−r=(1−r)²/4. Step 3: lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-subspace-closed (Mathlib Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional, FiniteDimension.lean:530) applies with exactly the hypotheses step 1 supplies (complete, nontrivially valued K; Hausdorff topological vector space). The proof takes an approximate minimizer with ‖z−w0‖<δ/s and never assumes the minimum is attained, which is correct without local compactness. Step 4: from w+ae=a(z−(w0−a⁻¹w)) the bound ‖w+ae‖≥s·max(‖w‖,|a|‖e‖) holds in all three cases. Step 5: the chain s·max(sM,|a|‖e‖)≥s²·max≥r·max holds, and V=W⊕Ke gives the basis. Edge cases n=0, n=1 and cancellation all check. Duplicate search: lem-sfb-finite-ultrametric-best-approximation and lem-sfb-ultrametric-orthogonal-extension give exact orthogonality only over finite E/Q_ℓ, where they rely on local compactness. They do not cover a general complete K, so they are not duplicates. No tool_uses and no SGA. One cosmetic point: the report mentions citations.json and searches.jsonl, which are not in the commit. No changes.
